structured.approach: I read the two contracted inputs, feat.tasks and org.engineering_stack, along with the DS-01 procedure from the data-science-steps skill. feat.tasks shows the Data Science lane's tasks, TSK-03 and TSK-04, change only ap_forecast. The step hook allows no shell commands, so I checked the repository through file reads instead of git commands. I read .git/HEAD, .git/config and the dev and main refs, the reflog of feature/story, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py, ci.py and tests/test_forecast.py. I compared what I found with the tool view (tool:repo-access), which states write access and a clean git status. No connector was needed. I wrote task.repo_access.md with the result, what the lane may do in the repository, three non-blocking open questions and a validation check.

claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) change only the ap_forecast repository.
Repository ap_forecast (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally, and the agent identity has write access with a clean git status.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, and HEAD is on feature/story.
Locally, dev and main point to the same commit, d67e8662907401467a3f76f9f167e7a60d89ffca.
Remote origin is configured, and local main and dev track it. There is no upstream entry for feature/story.
No repository creation is needed: the package src/ap_forecast with predict.py, explain.py and models.json already exists.
The current ap_forecast version is 0.9.0, and TSK-03 owns the version step.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. It enforces line coverage >= 90% and static checks that stand in for SonarQube.
The ci.py static checks flag print, eval and exec calls, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters. ci.py imports the coverage package.
No repository uses Databricks or a database, so no Databricks or other workspace access is required.
Commit messages start with the story ID, and branches follow main, dev and feature/<story>.
The agent may branch, commit, raise PRs and update defect status only: no merge, deploy or push to protected main.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): The working branch is literally named 'feature/story', but the convention is feature/<story> and this lane covers STORY-03 and STORY-04. Should the branch keep this name or be split or renamed per story? Interim answer: use the branch as created and keep the story ID as the commit prefix. Owner: Developer.

RAQ-2 (non-blocking): ci.py imports the third-party 'coverage' package. DS-01 allows no shell commands, so I could not check that it is installed for /usr/bin/python3. Interim answer: the first CI run in DS-05 or DS-06 confirms it. Owner: Developer / infra.
RAQ-3 (non-blocking): .git/config has no upstream for feature/story, so push rights on origin rest only on the tool view. Pushing is the spine's job. Owner: Spine / Developer.

The tool view says the agent has write access and git status is clean; I could not run git myself because this step allows no shell commands.
